question: Where is Morgan Stanley investing in technology for its advisors?

claims.text: Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley says it is making ongoing investments in its world-class platform, including investments to support its advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and the expansion of its workplace channel (period ended June 30, 2025).

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley names LeadIQ, its AI-powered lead distribution platform, which focuses on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with its financial advisors, as one of its early AI use cases (period ended September 30, 2025).
Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley names the DevGen AI tool, which enhances developer efficiency by modernizing code, as one of its early AI use cases (period ended September 30, 2025).
Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states that its scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools (period ended September 30, 2026).

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states it continues to invest in deepening its competitive moats in areas such as its expanded collaboration with Carta in private markets and in digital assets through announced partnerships with Zero Hash (period ended September 30, 2025).

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states it has put significant resources toward lending products, including digital tools, digital enhancements, and using automation to help with the paper backlog associated with various lending products (period ended March 31, 2026).
Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states it was overweighted to AI from the early days in wealth, including some of the work it did with OpenAI (period ended September 30, 2026).

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states that the insights from its size and scale allow its financial advisors to tailor advice and equip its own tools to deliver that advice to help clients achieve their goals (period ended September 30, 2026).

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states it continues to invest across its technology stack, embracing AI tools to support its infrastructure, business growth and people (period ended September 30, 2026).

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states it has been investing in its processes and systems across the technology side, in better understanding its data, and in better servicing its clients (period ended December 31, 2024).

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states that among its early AI use cases (some live and some in pilot) is LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform focused on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with its financial advisors (period 2025Q3).
Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states it is investing in products like LeadIQ that will allow it to match individuals with advisers (period 2026Q2).

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states it is using its scale to invest in broadening capabilities for financial advisors that are difficult for others to replicate: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending (period 2025Q4).

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states its wealth team is focused on AI 'co-piloting' where a financial adviser has historical context of past client interactions, and that the firm is building 'corridors' or 'super agents' to drive efficiency and effectiveness across the wealth portfolio (period 2026Q1).
Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states it continues to invest and deepen its competitive moats through an expanded collaboration with Carta in private markets (period 2025Q3).
Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states it continues to invest in digital assets through announced partnerships with Zero Hash (period 2025Q3).
Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley states its scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools (period 2026Q3).

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley's early AI use cases include LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform that matches workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitates engagement with its financial advisors (period ended September 30, 2025; Wealth Management scope). Why it might matter: the source says the cases were in pilot and showing progress. Why it might matter: Morgan Stanley says it is making ongoing investments to support its advisors through its world-class platform.

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley's CEO described 'co-piloting' for financial advisers, with Jed Finn under Andy Saperstein spending time on 'corridors or super agents' to drive efficiency and effectiveness across the wealth portfolio (period ended March 31, 2026; Wealth Management scope). Why it might matter: the source says the co-piloting gives a financial adviser historical context of past client interactions and how that might drive against certain market dynamics and future action.

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley is leveraging technology to improve automation and facilitate client acquisition openings, as well as increasing education with its advisors and clients (period ended December 31, 2025; Wealth Management scope). Why it might matter: the source says the growth reflects efforts to deepen client penetration with securities-based lending.

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley has ongoing investments in automation and AI, and in assessing where it wants its people over the next five to ten years, in the context of a reduction in XFA headcount (period ended March 31, 2025). Why it might matter: the source says the reduction of 3% of headcount XFAs in the first quarter came out of a rigorous year-end performance review assessment and process.

Morgan Stanley: CEO Edward Pick describes AI as a top priority for the firm's advisory role, saying the firm is now 'double overweight' on AI and that it is existentially important that Morgan Stanley be viewed as a trusted adviser in the middle of the ecosystem (period ended September 30, 2026).

Morgan Stanley: CFO Sharon Yeshaya describes early AI use cases, including LeadIQ, the firm's AI-powered lead distribution platform focused on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with its financial advisors, as well as DevGen AI (enhancing developer efficiency) and Parable (an interactive tool analyzing and summarizing data) (period ended September 30, 2025).
Morgan Stanley: CFO Sharon Yeshaya states the firm's scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools (period ended September 30, 2026).

Morgan Stanley: CEO Ted Pick states the firm is using its scale to invest in broadening capabilities for financial advisors that are difficult for others to replicate, including alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending (period ended December 31, 2025).

Morgan Stanley: CEO Edward Pick describes the ability to protect client assets and a resiliency theme as critical to clients, and states that although it is a people business, technology can help do a lot of the early work for financial advisers (period ended September 30, 2026).

Morgan Stanley: CEO Edward Pick describes the firm's world-class technology, world-class cyber defense and then the best trusted advisers sitting with the client as the secret sauce, including for the wealth management and financial adviser (period ended March 31, 2026).

Morgan Stanley: CEO Ted Pick states the firm continues to invest in Wealth, Institutional Securities, and Investment Management via human capital and technology, with growth plans embedding increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and client base (period ended December 31, 2025).

Morgan Stanley: CFO Sharon Yeshaya states the firm continues to invest across its technology stack, embracing AI tools to support its infrastructure, business growth and people (period ended September 30, 2026).

Morgan Stanley: CEO Edward Pick states cyber resiliency is a top priority across all of the firm's businesses, and that AI will bring efficiency and effectiveness that should not be dismissed as it transforms the firm (period ended March 31, 2026).
Morgan Stanley: CEO Edward Pick states the firm has built advantages against its advisor-led platform that make technology a differentiator in its favor (period ended September 30, 2026).

Morgan Stanley: CEO Ted Pick describes the early digital asset transformation in wealth, including a partnership with Zero Hash, expansion into crypto and tokenized asset capabilities, and continued work on the E*TRADE platform for the active self-directed community (period ended December 31, 2025).
